savings.title: Money style
savings.question: What's your money style right now?

options.title: Enjoy life
options.blurb: More fun now. Less of what's left goes to the future.

options.title: Balanced
options.blurb: Some for fun, a good chunk for later.

options.title: Save hard
options.blurb: Almost everything left after bills goes to the future.

invest.title: Where the money goes
invest.question: Where should your new savings go?

options.title: Play it safe
options.blurb: Mostly provident funds and deposits. Steady and boring.

options.title: A bit of everything
options.blurb: Shares for growth, provident funds and gold for cushion.

options.title: Go for growth
options.blurb: Mostly shares. Bigger swings, bigger upside over decades.

emergency.title: Emergency fund
emergency.question: How much cash will you keep for a rainy day?

options.title: Wing it
options.blurb: No separate cushion. Every spare rupee gets invested.

options.title: 3 months
options.blurb: Three months of bills sit in cash before you invest.

options.title: 6 months
options.blurb: Six months of bills in cash. Safe, but cash earns very little.

health.title: Health insurance
health.question: Will you buy your own health cover?

options.title: Rely on work's cover
options.blurb: Your employer's small cover is free, but it ends if you lose the job.

options.title: Basic cover
options.blurb: ₹5 lakh of cover. About ₹12,000 a year at 30, rising with age.

options.title: Strong cover
options.blurb: ₹25 lakh of cover. About ₹30,000 a year at 30, rising with age.

growth.title: Invest in yourself
growth.question: How much will you invest in getting better at what you do?

options.title: Coast
options.blurb: Do the job well. No extra courses or effort.

options.title: Keep learning
options.blurb: Some courses and mentors. Costs about 2% of your pay.

options.title: Go all in
options.blurb: Certifications, side projects, long evenings. Costs about 6% of your pay.

retire.title: Retirement age
retire.question: When do you want to stop working?

options.title: At 55
options.blurb: Early exit. Fewer years to earn, more to fund.

options.title: At 65
options.blurb: Keep going. More earning years, a shorter retirement.

provenance.basis: Illustrative game tuning: savings shares, learning cost as a share of pay, and the extra yearly pay growth each learning level buys. Not drawn from data. Replaced by the three-track capability model in v2. The three savings mixes are game presets; new savings follow the mix, existing holdings are never sold to rebalance. Insurance covers and premiums, and the emergency-fund sizes, are illustrative round numbers.
